title: Right-angle-free sets in the body-centred cubic crystal
statement: Let the body-centred cubic crystal B_N be the points (x, y, z) with 0 <= x, y, z <= 2N - 2 whose coordinates are all even (the N^3 corners of an (N-1) x (N-1) x (N-1) block of cubes of edge 2) or all odd (the (N-1)^3 cube centres); squared distance dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2, nearest neighbours at squared distance 3. Determine the largest number of points of the body-centred cubic crystal B_N such that no three of them form a right angle (no three points p, q, r with (q - p).(r - p) = 0), as a function of N. The exact values are known (ours) for N <= 3; the headline cell is N = 5: find 16 or more such points of the region of side 5.
submission: Text file: one point 'x y z' per line, a point of the region of side 5 (lines starting with # are ignored).
score: the number of points (larger is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: 15 points of the region of side 5 with no right angle (no three points p, q, r with (q - p).(r - p) = 0), the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)

context: A set of points is right-angle-free when no three of its points form a right angle. Gamble, Pulleyblank, Reed and Shepherd (1995) studied the largest right-angle-free subsets of the plane and of the square lattice, and related work (Junger and Pulleyblank) shows the problem NP-hard for general point sets; sets without isosceles right triangles in the n x n grid are a separate, active question (OEIS A271906; arXiv:2607.22828, 2026). In the body-centred cubic crystal the cube axes are perpendicular, and so are many face and body diagonals (for example (1, 1, 1) and (1, -1, 0)); how fast the largest right-angle-free sets grow is open.
references: B. Gamble, W. Pulleyblank, B. Reed, B. Shepherd, Right angle free subsets in the plane, Graphs and Combinatorics 11 (1995) 121-129
A Salem-Spencer-type construction for large subsets of integer grids with no isosceles right triangles, arXiv:2607.22828 (2026)
OEIS A271906 (largest subsets of the n x n grid with no right isosceles triangle)

novelty.verdict: new question for this lattice: right-angle-free subsets are studied for the square lattice (Gamble, Pulleyblank, Reed and Shepherd 1995; Junger and Pulleyblank) and isosceles right triangles in the square grid (A271906); no result was found for the body-centred cubic crystal, and it is not in the OEIS by name (too few exact values are known to search by terms).
closest: B. Gamble, W. Pulleyblank, B. Reed and B. Shepherd (1995): right-angle-free subsets of the plane and of the square lattice; another lattice.
OEIS A271906 and arXiv:2607.22828: no isosceles right triangle in the square grid, a weaker condition in another lattice.

baseline.text: 15 for N = 5, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: the points in `refs/bcc-right.txt` (the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)). Exact values for N = 2..3: 5, 9 (CP-SAT (OR-Tools 9.15, one worker) proved the optimum of the 0/1 model in tools/lattice_sets.py).
